rationale: The exposure is recorded for every discharge in the pharmacy system, and injurious falls are common enough in adults aged 70 and over (about 6 percent within 90 days) that following all discharges is efficient. A case-control design would add no efficiency and would make exposure timing relative to discharge harder to define. With nothing retrieved, the local cohort is also the only way to answer the question in this population.
alternatives: Case-control study of patients readmitted with a fall (refused: the outcome is not rare and exposure timing is clearer in a cohort)
Prospective cohort with new frailty assessment (refused: new data collection is outside the constraints)
Pragmatic trial of pharmacist deprescribing review (deferred: justified only if the cohort shows a meaningful association)
whyNotMoreComplex: A trial of deprescribing would answer the action question directly but needs funding and a signal worth testing; the cohort uses existing data to decide whether that signal exists.

decision.statement: Answer a narrowed question with a cohort built from existing data (injurious falls within 90 days after discharge for burden score 3 or more versus 0 to 2 in adults aged 70 and over) before any decision on routine deprescribing review.
decision.question: Is a high anticholinergic burden at discharge associated with injurious falls within 90 days after accounting for frailty?

criteria.text: The linked data contain enough injurious falls (about 300 or more in two years) to estimate a hazard ratio with useful precision.
A regional analysis using the same linked data has already answered the question.

gates.requirement: Information governance decision on whether linking pharmacy dispensing and regional admission records needs a new data access approval

alternatives: Stop routine scoring until regional guidance changes
decision.note: No ledger claim exists because the recorded search returned no records; the decision rests on the confirmed empty search and the investigator's local facts. The only gate stays unknown until the information governance office decides.

summary: Cohort recommended from existing data; the decision narrows the question and is blocked by one unknown data access gate.
